title: 'fix(axis): fix ticks overflowing grid area with dataZoom'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When dataZoom is applied, axis ticks near the visible edges can extend beyond the grid area and make a chart look visually broken even though the zoomed range itself is valid. Authors expect clipped or bounded ticks that stay inside the plotting region.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keep axis ticks contained within the grid when dataZoom changes the visible window, so zoomed charts look clean at the edges instead of drawing tick marks outside the plot area.


  ## Acceptance signals

  After zooming, edge ticks no longer overflow beyond the grid boundary, normal axis-tick rendering is preserved inside the plot, and unaffected non-zoomed charts keep their current appearance.'
=== bar-bordercolor-large-data ===
title: 'fix(bar): fix borderColor hides bar color with large data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Large bar-series rendering can lose the bar fill when `borderColor` is configured, making bars appear incorrectly outlined or visually empty. This is especially noticeable in dense charts where the large-data path is chosen automatically.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix the large-data bar rendering path so `borderColor` does not hide the bar’s actual fill color.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars rendered through the large-data path keep their fill color even when `borderColor` is set, border styling still applies as expected, and standard bar rendering remains unchanged.'
=== boxplot-encode-category-axis ===
title: 'fix(boxplot): correctly handle `series.encode` with category axis'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Boxplot charts can be driven from datasets and `series.encode`, but when a category axis is involved the encoded dimensions may be interpreted incorrectly. The result is a valid option that renders with misplaced or missing statistical boxes.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make boxplot series honor `series.encode` correctly on category axes so dataset-driven configurations map categories and box statistics to the intended dimensions.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A boxplot backed by dataset plus `series.encode` renders the expected categories and box values on a category axis, the encoded mapping no longer breaks the series, and existing boxplots without encode keep their current behavior.'

=== candlestick-non-normal-states ===
title: 'fix(candlestick): add back missing support for non-normal states since v5.0.0'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Candlestick charts support emphasis, blur, and select-style visual states, and users expect those non-normal states to continue working consistently across major versions. Since v5.0.0 some of that state handling was lost, so interactive styling no longer responds correctly.


  ## Desired outcome

  Restore the missing non-normal state support for candlestick series so hover, selection, and related state-based visuals behave again the way chart authors expect.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Candlestick items respond correctly in non-normal states, state-specific styling takes effect again without breaking normal rendering, and existing candlestick options keep their prior semantics.'
=== custom-renderitem-compoundpath ===
title: 'feat(custom): support compoundPath in custom series renderItem'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Custom-series authors sometimes need to return a composed path made from several subpaths as a single logical drawing element. Today `compoundPath` is not supported in `renderItem`, which blocks reusable vector shapes that are straightforward in lower-level graphics APIs.


  ## Desired outcome

  Support `compoundPath` as a valid custom-series element type so `renderItem` can return grouped path geometry in one element definition, provided `shape.paths` is supplied.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A custom series can return a `compoundPath` element from `renderItem`, `shape.paths` is honored when constructing the final graphic, and invalid compound definitions still fail clearly instead of silently misrendering.'
=== geojson-region-styling ===
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams who maintain their own GeoJSON files often want the map source itself to carry default presentation rules for specific regions, instead of forcing every chart option to restate those styles. At the moment, styling embedded directly in the GeoJSON is ignored, which makes shared map assets harder to reuse across multiple visualizations.

  ## Desired outcome

  When a GeoJSON region includes an `echartsStyle` property in its feature properties, ECharts should treat that as the region''s default styling for geo rendering. This should let authors ship map-specific visual defaults inside the original GeoJSON while still allowing chart configuration to build on top of those defaults where appropriate.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Region-level styles declared in GeoJSON `properties.echartsStyle` are reflected when the map is rendered through geo-based views, without requiring duplicate style configuration in every chart option. Existing GeoJSON files that do not define `echartsStyle` continue to render exactly as before.

  '
=== geojson-region-styling-2 ===
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors need region defaults embedded in GeoJSON to work consistently whether they use a standalone `geo` component or a `series.map`, and whether or not they explicitly list every region in `data` or `regions`. The initial GeoJSON styling support still leaves gaps in those map-series flows, especially when a region only exists in the source map and not in user-supplied series data.

  ## Desired outcome

  GeoJSON-defined region styling should become a first-class default across map usage, not just a geo-view special case. If a feature provides `properties.echartsStyle`, that style should flow into both `geo.regions` and `series.map` region models, including regions that need to be synthesized into the data so name-based lookup, rendering, and labels all remain complete.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A `series.map` can pick up `properties.echartsStyle` from the original GeoJSON even when the author did not manually add a matching data item for that region. The style participates in the normal region model pipeline instead of being a one-off view patch, so map rendering, labels, and region lookup stay consistent with other region options.

  '

title: 'fix(legend): fix legend action is not isolated from other legend components'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pages can contain multiple legend components, and actions intended for one legend should not silently affect another. Right now some legend operations leak across legend instances, causing unexpected selection changes elsewhere in the same chart.


  ## Desired outcome

  Isolate legend actions so each legend component responds only to the interactions and action payloads meant for it, even when several legends coexist in one option.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Triggering an action on one legend no longer changes unrelated legend components, targeted legend interaction still works, and existing single-legend charts behave the same as before.'

title: 'perf(line): reduce runtime memory cost'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Large line charts can put unnecessary pressure on the browser by holding more runtime memory than the renderer actually needs. Users feel this as slower interaction or higher memory usage rather than as a visible API problem.


  ## Desired outcome

  Reduce the runtime memory footprint of line-series rendering without changing chart appearance, public options, or event behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Equivalent line charts consume less memory during rendering or interaction, visual output remains unchanged, and no public configuration changes are required from chart authors.'
=== map-regions-silent ===
title: 'feat(map): support `regions[].silent` and update map data in tests'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Map authors sometimes need a region to remain visible but non-interactive, for example when a background territory should not respond to hover, selection, or tooltip behavior. ECharts already supports top-level `silent` behavior, but there is no reliable per-region contract for map and geo regions, so authors cannot selectively disable interaction on individual areas.

  ## Desired outcome

  Region configuration should support `silent` at the per-region level through `regions[].silent`, and that setting should be honored for both geo-based maps and `series.map` rendering. A region marked silent should keep its visual appearance while opting out of event handling and interactive affordances, without forcing the entire map to become non-interactive.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can declare `silent` on individual entries in `regions`, and the targeted region becomes non-interactive while neighboring regions continue to respond normally. The contract applies consistently to rendered GeoJSON regions and SVG-backed regions, and map data refreshes should preserve the updated region behavior instead of losing it when the source map data changes.

  '
=== marker-formatter-series-context ===
title: 'fix(marker): fix marker label formatter can''t get series information'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When chart authors customize marker labels with formatter callbacks, they expect to receive the same series context that other formatter-based APIs expose. For mark points, lines, and areas, that context can currently be incomplete, which prevents formatter logic from reliably reading series information.


  ## Desired outcome

  Ensure marker label formatter callbacks receive the related series metadata consistently so custom label text can depend on the originating series without hacks or duplicated state.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A marker label formatter can read the expected series information when building label text, the callback contract is consistent across marker types, and existing marker rendering remains unchanged when no custom formatter is used.'

=== master-into-v6 ===
title: 'chore: merge master into v6'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The v6 release branch needs regular synchronization with ongoing master development so maintainers can keep packaging, fixes, and infrastructure aligned. This is branch-management work, not a new user-visible feature.


  ## Desired outcome

  Merge the relevant master changes into the v6 branch while preserving the expected public behavior of the release line and avoiding regressions introduced by branch drift.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The v6 branch reflects the intended upstream updates, the merge does not invent a new standalone feature requirement of its own, and user-facing behavior is whatever the merged source already defines.'
=== pictorial-zero-value-flipping ===
title: 'fix(pictorial): fix zero value flipping for different axes'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using `pictorialBar` with image or path symbols expects zero-valued items to stay visually anchored without suddenly mirroring in the wrong direction. After the earlier zero-value fix, some axis combinations still render a flipped symbol when the chart changes between horizontal and vertical layouts or uses inverse axes, so the same data can look wrong depending on orientation.

  ## Desired outcome

  Zero-valued pictorial bars should keep a stable, sensible symbol direction across horizontal and vertical charts, including inverse-axis layouts. A value of zero must no longer trigger an accidental flip simply because the axis orientation or inversion changes.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The zero-value rendering is correct for all four combinations covered by chart authors in practice: horizontal, horizontal with inverse axis, vertical, and vertical with inverse axis. Non-zero pictorial bars continue to render with their existing direction logic, and the fix applies equally to custom image symbols and path-based symbols.

  '
=== pictorialbar-zero-symbol-flip ===
title: 'fix(pictorialBar): symbol should not flip with zero data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pictorial bar charts can use symbol direction and orientation to express meaning, but a zero value should not invert that symbol unexpectedly. Right now hitting zero can flip the symbol, producing a misleading visual jump at exactly the point where no bar should extend.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keep pictorial-bar symbols from flipping when the data value is zero so orientation stays stable across zero-valued points.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A zero-value pictorial bar preserves the expected symbol direction, nearby positive or negative values still render with their intended orientation rules, and zero no longer introduces a special-case flip.'
=== pie-label-visibility ===
title: 'fix(pie): fix some labels may not show'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pie charts with dense labels can occasionally hide labels that should remain visible, causing important categories to disappear from the rendered result even though there is enough room for them in the final layout. Authors experience this as an intermittent labeling bug rather than a configuration mistake.


  ## Desired outcome

  Correct the pie-label layout logic so labels that should be shown are not incorrectly dropped during collision handling or final positioning.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The previously missing pie labels render consistently in the affected layout, other overlap-avoidance behavior still works, and unchanged configurations do not gain stray duplicate labels.'
=== polar-coordinate-clipping ===
title: 'fix(polar): fix unexpected clipping in polar coordinate'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Charts in polar coordinates can clip content that should remain visible, producing truncated graphics near the edges even when the data and series configuration are valid. Authors see this as unexpected cropping rather than an intentional bound.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix polar-coordinate clipping so series content is only clipped where it should be, and valid shapes are not cut off unexpectedly by the rendering bounds.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected polar chart renders without the unwanted clipping artifact, legitimate boundary clipping still works where necessary, and non-polar charts are unaffected.'

=== release-back-merge ===
title: Merge release back to master
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The release branch needs to stay aligned with ongoing mainline work without changing the already-shipped contracts in surprising ways. This merge is repository maintenance rather than a discrete user-facing feature request.


  ## Desired outcome

  Bring the release branch back in sync with the current master branch contents while preserving the intended public behavior of the v6 line and avoiding accidental regressions in packaging, types, or chart rendering.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The branch contains the expected upstream changes after the merge, no standalone new requirement is introduced beyond synchronization itself, and public behavior remains the one defined by the merged source.'
=== release-v5-6-0 ===
title: Release v5.6.0
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  ECharts is ready for its 5.6.0 release and downstream users need a publishable package that reflects the latest completed work across chart behavior, geo/map handling, visualMap interaction, rendering fixes, and localization assets. This is release engineering rather than a new end-user feature, but it is the step that turns the accumulated changes into something consumers can install and ship.

  ## Desired outcome

  Prepare the 5.6.0 release so the distributed bundles, package metadata, and generated assets all match the current source state. The published package should identify itself as version `5.6.0`, depend on `zrender` `5.6.1`, and include the newly generated locale bundles such as `langFA` and `langSV`, while preserving the user-visible behavior delivered by the merged fixes and features in this release.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The release artifacts and package metadata are internally consistent for version `5.6.0`, the generated distribution files are rebuilt from current sources, and the added locale bundles are available to consumers in the shipped package. This remains a packaging and release update, so no previously documented public API or runtime behavior should regress beyond the intentional changes already included in the release.

  '
=== stepped-line-area-nulls ===
title: 'fix(line): fix areaStyle skewing in stepped line series and incorrect connectNull behavior'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Stepped line charts with area fills can render distorted polygons, and series that combine stepped lines with null data may connect points in ways authors did not intend. The result is a visibly wrong chart even though the series option is valid.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix stepped line rendering so `areaStyle` follows the step geometry correctly and `connectNull` respects gaps in the same way users expect from the stepped path, including edge cases where null values sit near step transitions.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A stepped line with `areaStyle` no longer shows skewed fill geometry, null gaps are connected only when `connectNull` should apply, and the stepped series path stays visually consistent with its data order.'
=== visualmap-handle-label-collision ===
title: 'fix(visualMap): handle label collides with horizontal size visualMap'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A horizontal size visualMap can place its handle label in the same space as nearby UI, causing collisions that make the control hard to read or awkward to interact with. The overlap is a layout bug in a common dashboard configuration.


  ## Desired outcome

  Improve horizontal size-visualMap layout so the handle label avoids colliding with surrounding control elements and remains readable without manual spacing hacks from the chart author.


  ## Acceptance signals

  In the affected horizontal size visualMap layout, the handle label no longer overlaps the conflicting UI, the control stays legible and usable, and other visualMap layouts keep their current behavior.'
